_comment: GH#324 A/B — THE dead-render repro, kept as a live regression capture. A talk_pool bark interacted at world_ready+0 vs +90 idle frames, same ROOM, same run (leg B moved off the clerk 2026-08-03 -- see leg B's own note; the A/B has always been bark-panel-vs-bark-panel, never NPC identity). BEFORE the fix, shot 01 was an empty line slot while ui_dialogue_rendered carried the full string (three maps, pre-existing); the cause was NOT rendering but the evidence boundary — a transient panel's windowed-QA hold is a 0.4s wall-clock floor while a capture settles 0.15s PLUS up to 3s of live-tween drain (#119), and the boot music crossfade (1.0s) reliably pushed the capture past the floor. Measured on this very script: settle 817ms at world_ready+0 vs 226ms at +90, against a 400ms hold. test_driver now holds transient panels while a capture is in flight (TestDriver.capture_in_flight), so BOTH legs render. `assert_dialogue_displayed` is the assertion half — it reads message_layer's live panel state at capture time, so a regression fails loud instead of quietly shipping an empty PNG. WINDOWED ONLY (headless skips both the shots and the probe, by construction). CANONICAL since the v0.17 train -- registered in qa/manifest.json and the AGENTS.md seed table at seed 9, tier full. The older note in this slot (screenshot utility, title_peek/street_peek's class, deliberately absent from the manifest) predated that promotion and was already false on main; corrected here rather than left to mislead the next reader. Seed inert: no fight resolves.

steps._comment: == LEG B: the control — a talk_pool bark in the same room, same run, 90 idle frames later. This one always rendered; it is here so the pair reads as one A/B, not two claims. TARGET MOVED 2026-08-03 (#318, W3): the clerk now carries a `conversation` as well as his pool, so his SECOND interact opens a graph instead of re-serving a bark (interactions.gd's npc arm consults `social_talked` first) — a graph panel is a DIFFERENT panel and would have silently changed what this capture proves. The mechanism under test is the capture-hold boundary on a TRANSIENT bark panel, not this particular speaker, so leg B moves to the room's other pool NPC and the A/B is intact. ROBUSTNESS, since stationer_client ALSO carries a conversation: this is leg B's FIRST interact with her, and interactions.gd's npc arm serves the pool bark on ANY first interact regardless of an attached graph (it consults social_talked before conversation), so a future lane attaching a graph in this room cannot break this leg -- only a SECOND interact on the same NPC inside one waking can, which is exactly what broke the old target. OWNERSHIP: this file is a message_layer pin and sits in W4's OWNS, not W3's. The edit is forced by #318 and is recorded in W3's .lane-progress SEAMS for the merge train. ==
